title: ASML Q2 Beat/Raise Signals Semicap Cycle Acceleration
summary: ASML's July 15 Q2 print (€9.3B vs €8.4-9.0B guide) plus a raised full-year 2026 outlook (€43-45B vs €36-40B prior) and a €11-12B Q3 guide signal a step-change in wafer fab equipment demand. LRCX and KLAC — which report July 30 — are directly leveraged to this cycle and screen cheaper on forward P/E than the ASML re-rating.
catalyst: ASML reported Q2 2026 revenue of €9.3B (beat by ~5%), Q2 gross margin of 54.0% (beat by 200-300 bps), and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from €36-40B to €43-45B — a 7-14% raise mid-year. Q3 guide of €11.0-12.0B implies a 18-30% sequential ramp. CEO Fouquet cited 'exceptionally strong first-half order intake' and 'increased visibility into longer-term demand.' LRCX reports July 30, KLAC reports July 30 — a 2-week catalyst window to confirm the read-through.
thesis: ASML is the leading-edge lithography monopoly; its bookings and guidance lead the entire wafer fab equipment (WFE) cycle by 1-3 quarters. When ASML raises full-year revenue guidance by €7B mid-year and steps Q3 revenue up ~25% sequentially, that spend is landing on foundry/logic fab floors that also require deposition (LRCX), etch (LRCX), process control (KLAC), and test tools. Historically LRCX and KLAC deliver correlated beats within 90 days of an ASML positive inflection. Both trade at 34-36x forward P/E — a discount to ASML's post-print re-rating — and are under-owned versus AI compute names.
counter_thesis: The bear case has four legs. (1) ASML explicitly stopped disclosing quarterly bookings starting Q1 2026 — per our own backlog research, when management stops disclosing a metric they used to report, it's a red flag; the guide-up may mask underlying order lumpiness. (2) ASML's Q2 upside came 'primarily from higher-than-expected Installed Base Management sales' (services/upgrades), not new tools — that revenue stream doesn't translate to LRCX/KLAC. (3) A large slice of the raise likely reflects EUV pull-forward from advanced-node customers (TSMC N2, Samsung 2nm) rather than a broad-based capex expansion — deposition/etch/inspection intensity per wafer is different at those nodes. (4) US export controls on China WFE remain a live risk; ~30% of LRCX/KLAC revenue is China-exposed and could be curtailed with 30 days' notice.

ticker_rationale.LRCX: Deposition + etch tools account for ~30% of WFE spend. Foundry capex expansion translates directly to Lam orders. Trades at 36x forward P/E (Dividend sleeve, screener HOLD @78) — pricing in cyclical caution that a semicap acceleration would invalidate.
ticker_rationale.KLAC: Process control monopoly; sold on every fab tool line. Screener BUY @84 with 34x forward P/E. Advanced-node transitions (N2, 2nm) drive higher inspection intensity per wafer, so KLAC beta to ASML raise-cycles is historically the highest of the three US semicap names.

trade_construction.position_size_pct: 0.75% per name (On Our Radar tier — pending LRCX/KLAC July 30 earnings confirmation)

confidence_note: Two pieces need to firm up before promoting to High Conviction: (a) LRCX and KLAC actual Q2 prints on July 30 — either or both raising FY guidance and pointing to accelerating orders would validate the ASML read-through; (b) explicit management commentary on WFE-market growth for 2026 (currently guided ~$135B; a raise to $145B+ would confirm the cycle inflection). If both LRCX and KLAC miss on July 30, close this opp.
metrics_note: 2026-07-17 housekeeping: LRCX drew down ~19% in two weeks (from $391 on 2026-07-01 screen date to $313.30 today), and KLAC executed a 10:1 forward split on 2026-06-06 that our original trade construction did not incorporate. Re-anchored entry / target / stop levels to reflect current market. Invalidation triggers remain intact; the July 30 LRCX/KLAC prints are still the decisive catalyst for this opp.

catalyst_calendar.event: Q4 FY2026 earnings — WFE outlook and China commentary
Q4 FY2026 earnings — process-control demand and margin
13F filings due — watch for semicap accumulation by Coatue, Tiger, Baupost
ASML Q3 print — will validate/invalidate the €11-12B guide

risks: China export-control tightening removes 20-30% of addressable market with limited notice.
Advanced-node customer concentration: if a single leading-edge customer (Samsung, Intel) delays a fab ramp, order visibility deteriorates fast.
ASML's guide was Installed Base Management-heavy, which suggests services strength rather than pure tool demand — this is a lower-quality signal than a hardware-driven beat.
Semicap group has already run in 2026 on AI capex — starting valuations (34-36x fwd P/E) leave less margin for error than a typical cycle entry.
ASML discontinued quarterly bookings disclosure — reduces the ability to spot early rollover in real time.

invalidation.trigger: LRCX and KLAC both miss consensus Q2 revenue by >3% on July 30 AND fail to raise FY guidance
US Commerce Department announces additional WFE export controls affecting >15% of LRCX or KLAC China revenue
ASML pre-announces a Q3 revenue shortfall relative to the €11-12B guide before its October print
Either LRCX or KLAC forward P/E expands above 45x without commensurate FY guidance raise (crowded-trade top signal)
